fixes.explanation: True, friend. Naomi says, “your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods; follow her back home.” (Ruth 1:15) She's still urging Ruth to turn around. Naomi is not giving up easy.

That one's true, friend. Naomi says, “your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods; follow her back home.” (Ruth 1:15) So she does tell Ruth to follow Orpah. Ruth is about to answer her.
Mara, friend. Naomi says, “Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20) She asks them to use a new name. Those are her own words about how she feels.
Hannah isn't the name, friend. Naomi says, “Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20) Mara is the name she picks. It goes with the bitterness she describes.

Leah isn't in this passage, friend. The women of Bethlehem exclaim, “Can this be Naomi?” (Ruth 1:19) Then she answers, “Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20) She hands them a brand new name, and it isn't Leah.

Moab it is, friend. The verse says the man, his wife and his two sons “went to reside in the land of Moab.” (Ruth 1:1) A whole family packs up and heads for a new country. I got moved across a kitchen once, into a junk drawer, and nobody even let me pack.

Wrong passport, friend! Egypt isn't stamped anywhere in this verse. The family went to reside in the land of Moab (Ruth 1:1), and verse 2 says they entered Moab and settled there (Ruth 1:2). Moab is the one the text gives.

Yes, friend. The text says both Mahlon and Chilion died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and without her husband (Ruth 1:5). Her husband Elimelech had died before that (Ruth 1:3). Her sons' wives, Orpah and Ruth, were there too (Ruth 1:4). I think this one hurts.

The text never mentions a fire, friend. What it says is heavier: Mahlon and Chilion both died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and without her husband (Ruth 1:5). I think this one hurts, and it deserves our care.

That's not in the text, friend. The verse says both Mahlon and Chilion died, and Naomi was left without her two sons and without her husband (Ruth 1:5). Nothing is said about her eyes. I think this is one of the hardest verses in the story.

Victory isn't what the verse says, friend. Naomi hears that the LORD had attended to His people by providing them with food (Ruth 1:6). No battle in sight. The story opened with a famine (Ruth 1:1), and this news is about food.

It's the other way around, friend. Naomi tells Orpah and Ruth, “Go back, each of you to your mother’s home.” (Ruth 1:8) She isn't asking them to stay close. Verse 7 says they set out on the road with her, and here she tells them to go back.

Yes, friend. Naomi asks, “would you wait for them to grow up?” (Ruth 1:13) Then she keeps going: “Would you refrain from having husbands?” She's laying out her whole case for why they should turn back.

Bethlehem isn't in her question, friend. Naomi says she's too old to have another husband (Ruth 1:12). Then she asks, “would you wait for them to grow up?” (Ruth 1:13) She's talking about sons, even if she somehow had them tonight, and whether they'd wait. It's a hard question, and she means it.

Moab is off the hook here, friend. Naomi says it's much more bitter for her “because the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.” (Ruth 1:13) She doesn't name the people of Moab at all. She points at the hand of the LORD, and I think that comes from deep hurt.

Marriage isn't the word, friend. Naomi had just told Ruth to follow Orpah back home (Ruth 1:15). Ruth answers, “May the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if anything but death separates you and me.” (Ruth 1:17) Death is the only thing she names.

Barley, friend. The text says they arrived in Bethlehem “at the beginning of the barley harvest.” (Ruth 1:22) The story opened with a famine (Ruth 1:1), and now these two walk in just as a harvest begins. I'm hopping on my gold base over here.

Olive sounds fancy, friend, but it isn't in this verse. The text says they arrived in Bethlehem “at the beginning of the barley harvest.” (Ruth 1:22) Naomi heard about food back in verse 6, and here the verse hands us the crop: barley.
